##### Project general facts

Azalea is a villa community by Emaar, designed in a contemporary Arabesque style with warm-coloured tiled roofs, eaves and subtle trimmings. The collection comprises three, four and five bedroom villas with spacious rooms, a carport and pockets of greenery between the homes.

Residents enjoy access to a neighbourhood pool and park, while the wider Arabian Ranches lifestyle includes a residents' club with a gym, swimming pool, beauty salon and spa. A golf course, polo grounds, tennis courts, football pitches, landscaped gardens and a gourmet restaurant are close at hand. A school, a mosque and a retail centre sit next to the community.

Interiors feature wooden finishes, polished marble floors and architectural stone details. Kitchens are fitted with clean-lined cabinetry, and the master bedroom includes an en suite bathroom.

##### Location description and benefits

Arabian Ranches II is a master-planned residential area in Dubailand, set along Al Qudra Road with quick access to Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Emirates Road. The neighbourhood is known for its green landscaping, tree-lined streets and calm, resort-style atmosphere, while remaining well connected to Downtown Dubai, Dubai Marina and Al Maktoum International Airport.

Daily needs are covered by the Arabian Ranches Community Centre and the Ranches Souk, with supermarkets, cafés, pharmacies and clinics close by. Respected schools such as Jumeirah English Speaking School and Ranches Primary School serve the area, and Motor City, Dubai Studio City, Dubai Sports City and Global Village are a short drive away. The Arabian Ranches Golf Club and the Dubai Polo and Equestrian Club add leisure options on the doorstep.

The area attracts steady demand from families and long-term tenants looking for spacious homes in a green, secure setting, which supports stable rental returns and resale values. Property here is freehold and open to international buyers, making Arabian Ranches II a popular choice for end users and investors alike.
